Okay so my last comment was removed for being too short. So I am writing to tell you that there is a place where you can watch movies on demand for free as long as you have a library card. Also, your library needs to be a participating library. Hopefully I have written enough filler text here to tell you that you should check out Hoopla.

I typically use a fly fish lure.

But seriously, if you want the legal route either hunt down cheap DVDs, or scour the streaming services. They actually have absolutely massive libraries but the old stuff rarely comes to the front u less you start actively looking for it. 

Max has a really incredible older library. Netflix is ok. Amazon has a lot of paid content. FreeVee I think has a decent older library. 

You just need to figure out what you want to watch. Even just find one movie on a service, then use the watch similar features to find other stuff. Jump in and out of various movies to find variety. Then watch a few, figure out what you like, then do searches for similar movies. 

Then you're off to the races!

Check your local library. There are tons of movies they don't have, but there are tons of movies they might have that aren't available to stream anywhere (legally). Stuff that's only ever been available on DVD/blu-ray, out of print DVDs, your library might have it. If your library doesn't have it and it's only available on physical media, your library might take suggestions on future purchases. Your library might also have some streaming services (Hoopla and Kanopy) that occasionally have stuff that's not available anywhere else.

Libraries certainly don't have everything, but you might be surprised at what they do have. Especially if you live in a large enough city.

There’s a real hole in the streaming marketplace for catalogue titles that is not being filled. Sites like Paramount Plus control large libraries but only allow a trickle of titles onto the platform every month. Criterion has a lot, but their library is almost exclusively art house. Free sites like Tubi and Freevee are worthwhile. They have a ton of older genre content. Library sites like Kanopy and Hoopla are very well curated and have lots of good stuff, but there is a limit to how many titles you can stream per month. One thing I do is budget a little money to rent the occasional must see movie from Amazon or iTunes.
For sure.  I've also gotta shout out [Leonid Gaidai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonid_Gaidai#Filmography) who I would probably not even know about if not for that channel.

The real answer is piracy. There are always movies that can’t be found on any streaming service, and you either have to rent or buy. An example of this is L’Atalante from 1934, which can’t be streamed with any subscription. Piracy gives you what you want, on demand whenever you want it, and in the best quality. In July last year the movie *Psycho* was on Netflix, in horrible DVD resolution. For a while you may think that your movie needs can be satisfied by some amalgamation of HBO Max, Criterion Channel, and Kanopy and TCM. Do not believe it. Nothing will bring you peace but piracy.

I have a lot of luck using Kanopy and also going through the public library. If your country branch doesn't have what you're looking for, there may be programs that they can access from other services/library systems through things like inter-library loan.
In addition to what others have said, check out [Archive.org](https://Archive.org), their visual media stock. Now, a ton of their stuff is unrestored, but often there are pleasant surprises.

I wholeheartedly agree. Furthermore, finding obscure, or often not even obscure but popular foreign films can be impossible through streaming services. Criterion is a rare exception I can think of off the top of my head, yet you’re still limited to their rotating catalogue.

Get a VPN (I recommend Mullvad), download qBittorrent, and learn how to search for torrents online. Add in VLC media player and also OpenSubtitles.com for foreign films and you’re golden. It has genuinely been the most helpful skill in enjoying my hobby of watching films that I’ve learned.

It seems hard at first, but the learning curve really isn’t that steep. On top of that, knowing that you have the files to that film permanently is really nice, and being able to spread it around to others around the globe through torrent seeding is a beautiful thing. I should mention, get ready to upgrade your storage if you really dive into it.

Tube has a surprisingly large collection of old films. I watched some films from the 20s-40 that I couldn’t get my hands on otherwise. 

Mubi also streams a lot of older films, especially art house and some classics. 

You can also get films at second hand dvd shops.

Piracy is such a loaded term. It was probably coined by large commercial interests who wanted to discourage the public from not paying them. Fuck them.

Today you can find many websites, that offer all the movies ever made in history, available for free viewing. I can’t imagine ever paying a company like Netflix or Disney money for “subscriptions”. Fuck them.

Anybody interested, DM me I’ll hook you up.

Piracy hasn’t brought me peace. Sure, it brought me a collection of over 700 films from the auteur canon, almost all in Blu-Ray remux quality. But I lie awake at night wondering when the torrent for that one obscure Godard film, or my one missing Rivette film, is finally going to get seeded. I have hit the limits of public trackers, and I just don’t have the upload capacity for private trackers.

I second the library! And Kanopy! Its free!

Yeah, me neither, sometimes. I’ve been thinking about finding a way to join the PTP tracker but it seems like too much work, and too much uploading. 

However I have seen every Rivette film (other than Out 1), so the one you couldn’t find must be out there somewhere. A lot of the time, movies that aren’t being seeded can otherwise be found on archive.org or YouTube. As a public service I tend to upload more obscure films onto Internet Archive once I’ve downloaded them. Someday, though, I’ll make it a personal project to join one of the prestigious private trackers, because they’re the only ones who have DVD rips with commentary tracks.

My missing *Rivette* film is *L’amour par terre*. I have a torrent for a copy of the Blu-Ray stuck at 68% for months. I want to see the film that way, because the old DVD release is a very bad transfer.

I have seen *Out 1* since the Blu-Rays have been uploaded to one major open community a couple of years ago. Interesting, but unlike *Satantango*, it is not an experience I think I’ll ever repeat.

>Unfortunately they seem to have a limited library that recycles every couple months.

I think that's a little unfair.  Yes, certain titles recycle, but some titles pop up and then don't play again for a long time (or sometimes never again).   Unless you go through the schedule day-by-day you might miss some of those more uncommon items.  (And if you're accessing just a subset of TCM via elsewhere then obviously you'll see even less.)
